title: Claiborne Williams' big band at the dances
summary: Harold recalls dances in 1929 where the Donaldsonville band of Claiborne Williams, with son George, was hired.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: And after, like they used to give the dancers a long time ago that we know, and they had all the top bands used to come there and play. And like when we'd come in town, that was in 1929 when we'd give a dance and bagged up, and like I said before, they loved Claiborne Williams, some from Donaldsonville.
Did they hire him all the way from Donaldsonville? Yeah, sure, sure, of course.
They know he was going to make the money.
Did he have a big band?

Yeah, he had a big band. He had a 12-piece band. He played the violin, you know. And his son George Williams was a fine saxophone player. He was a culture musician, he was good. In the Navy he was playing trumpet and piano. Good piano player, good musician, good arranger. But that was the days of the big band and they had some good bands.
